claims.text: The Pulumi for Terraform Users guide teaches how to reference existing Terraform state files from Pulumi, use any Terraform provider in Pulumi programs, import and use Terraform modules directly, convert HCL code to Pulumi, and orchestrate both Terraform and Pulumi deployments together.
Any Terraform provider can be used in Pulumi programs.
Terraform modules can be imported and used directly in Pulumi.
`new pulumi.StackReference("core-infra")` with `getOutput("vpcId")` retrieves an output from another Pulumi stack.

Pulumi provides a `terraform.state.S3Reference` resource (from `@pulumi/terraform`, also accessed as `pulumi.terraform.state.S3Reference`) that takes `bucket` and `key` arguments to reference Terraform state stored in S3 and exposes `getOutput`.

The `terraform.state.S3Reference` example uses a 'terraform' namespace without importing it in the multi-stack example; the Terraform state reference resource in Pulumi is named `terraform.state.RemoteStateReference` with a `backendType` of s3.
The `aws.ecs.Cluster` resource accepts a `configuration.executeCommandConfiguration` argument with `kmsKeyId` and `logging` properties, where `logging` accepts the value "DEFAULT".
`pulumi import` can be used to bring Terraform-managed resources under Pulumi management.
`pulumi import` takes the form `pulumi import <type-token> <name> <id>`, e.g. `pulumi import aws:ec2/vpc:Vpc main-vpc vpc-12345`.
Pulumi supports transferring state ownership gradually, resource-by-resource, from Terraform to Pulumi.

A migration helper that calls `getOutput("resources")` on an S3Reference and filters by resource type to import resources is a viable approach; the Pulumi import API can be used programmatically to import resources.
Pulumi policies (Policy as Code) can enforce infrastructure policies that work across both Terraform and Pulumi resources.

`@pulumi/policy` exports `PolicyPack` and `validateResourceOfType`; policies accept `name`, `description`, `enforcementLevel` ("mandatory") and `validateResource` with a `(resource, args, reportViolation)` callback.
The `aws.s3.Bucket` resource has an `acl` property that can be "public-read" or "public-read-write".
The Pulumi Automation API allows embedding Pulumi in applications for dynamic infrastructure management.

The Pulumi Automation API is imported from `@pulumi/pulumi/automation` and provides `LocalWorkspace.createOrSelectStack` (with `stackName`, `projectName`, `program`), `stack.setConfig`, and `stack.up({ onOutput })` which returns an object with `outputs`.
Component resources can integrate with Terraform behind the scenes, leaving the complexity of multi-tool management to the platform team rather than development teams.
`pulumi.ComponentResource` subclasses call `super(type, name, {}, opts)` with a type token such as "custom:WebApplication", and use `registerOutputs`.
